content.knowledge_point: Finding the Pivot Columns of a Matrix
content.problem:
What are the pivot columns of the matrix $P,$ given by

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 & 1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -4 & 5 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]?
$$
content.worked_solution:
First, we need to convert $P$ to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 & 1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -4 & 5 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 & 1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & -4 & 5 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & ↔{R}_{4} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 & 1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & -4 & 5 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Looking at the row echelon form, we see that $P$ has $4$ pivots. In particular, the pivot columns are the $1$st, $2$nd, $3$rd, and $4$th columns.
